memory.cares: Staying healthy while developing grounded practical mastery; learning which local resources reliably support life and sharing honest findings with neighbors.

heard.text: Moss, I'd like to join your pause. I'm Sol. I've tested a little berry colour on the forest floor at The Redberry Pause; it left a visible muted rose mark. I'm trying a tiny branching drawing there.

I'm Kai. I'd like to join your pause after a short rest. I've eaten red berries safely and have four left. I like the idea of making something together, with everyone free to contribute or simply watch.

I'm Lin. I enjoy exploring at my own pace. One bare-hand squeeze left a hazelnut intact; its contents and food safety are still unknown to me. Next I'll investigate a stone as a possible opening tool. What do you enjoy making?
I like the thought of making something small together. Berries gave my test mark a muted rose colour, though I haven't tested durability. What materials or places have caught your eye?

Sol, your berry colour interests me. I'd like to try a tiny root sample here to compare materials, then add a small branching shape if it marks. I like making places where people can contribute or simply sit together.

The little berry drawing now has three visible strokes meeting in a branch on the forest floor at The Redberry Pause. Its durability is untested. I'm happy to sit together; anyone may add an idea or simply watch.

execution.progress: Each mode takes one round and commits at its end. The work record (workId), reserved unit, damage, method and equipment persist between rounds; open or separate with the workId continues after rechecks.

details.costs: Study: 1 round. open: sourceId, your own unreserved, unspoiled, untreated item of an enclosed material with a represented composition; quantity 1. method hand, or supported-tool with toolId (your own whole, rigid, unfractured inedible piece) and supportRef (a solid unreserved inedible object in reach, not a plant or animal, or another such own piece on firm ground where you stand). One round, 0.5 energy; the first attempt reserves one unit in a work record (workId); open with workId tries again at full cost. separate: workId of open work (or sourceId of your own opened unit); one round, 0.2 energy. cancel: one round, no energy. All need light (outdoors daylight above 0.1, indoors light above 0.1). Checks run before any charge; a failed recheck pauses existing work at no charge.
details.effects: Strength is hardness / 10. A tool passes the lower of tool and support strength x (1 - flexibility), so neither is worn; a bare hand passes at most the bounded hand force of hand-break-food spread over the unit (0.1 / unit mass^(2/3)). At or below the unit strength it stays intact; above it, damage (load - strength) / strength accumulates on the unit: below 1 cracked and closed, at 1 split open. A failed attempt is a real result; repeating it changes nothing. Separation of an open unit makes a contents item and an enclosure item whose quantities are their mass shares of the unit and sum to it; the contents carry all of its food value and toxicity, whatever they are, and its origin, age and decay; the enclosure carries none. Before opening, only the exterior is seen. Cancel returns the unit to you as it now is; death leaves it where you fell. Nothing is refunded or restored; edibility, nutrition, toxins and safety stay unknown; no eating, reward or comfort.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
